opened_sources.result: Opened. IAU defines the 88 constellations as bounded sky areas, distinguishes figures/asterisms from those areas, and lists Centaurus/Cen, Dorado/Dor, Tucana/Tuc and Ursa Minor/UMi.

Opened. NASA gives Omega Centauri as a globular cluster in Centaurus, 17,700 light-years away, roughly 10 million gravitationally bound stars, and reports more than 500 Hubble images over two decades finding seven fast-moving inner stars as compelling IMBH evidence.

Opened. NASA identifies 30 Doradus/Tarantula as an emission nebula in the Large Magellanic Cloud at about 170,000 light-years; UV radiation and hot particles from young stars hollowed the gas bubble and compressed its rim into ridges.
Opened. NASA identifies the bright dot above the Small Magellanic Cloud as NGC 104/47 Tucanae, a globular cluster of hundreds of thousands of stars in Tucana.

Opened. NASA APOD gives 47 Tuc about 13,000 light-years and the Small Magellanic Cloud about 210,000 light-years, explicitly saying they are not physically close; it identifies the SMC as a Milky Way satellite galaxy.

Opened. NASA places Polaris near the north celestial pole, says it traces a small 24-hour circle and is useful for north; it is the Little Dipper handle/tail in Ursa Minor, is not the sky's brightest star, and gives Vega as poleward about 14,000 years ago and again about 12,000 years in the future.

articles.evidence: IAU supports Cen and the sky-area distinction. NASA supports Centaurus location, 17,700 ly, roughly 10 million bound stars, and the more-than-500-image/seven-fast-star IMBH-evidence account. The wording preserves the candidate/evidence qualification.
IAU supports Dor and the sky-area distinction. NASA supports 30 Doradus/Tarantula as an emission nebula in the LMC at about 170,000 ly and the UV/hot-particle bubble, compressed-ridge explanation.

IAU supports Tuc and the sky-area distinction. NASA TESS supports the bright NGC 104/47 Tuc dot above the SMC; NASA APOD supports the 13,000/210,000 ly comparison, halo/satellite-galaxy distinction, and lack of physical proximity.

articles.finding: The final temporal sentence is self-contradictory and reverses the cited source's future interval: it says 'около 14 000 лет назад ... будет ближе к Веге'.
articles.required_correction: Replace it with: 'Около 14 000 лет назад небесный полюс был направлен к Веге; примерно через 12 000 лет он снова будет у Веги.' This preserves NASA's distinct past and future statements. The rest of the Polaris explanation is supported.
